name: Medes
place: Ecbatana in the Zagros, western Iran
desc: Iranian horsemen of the Zagros valleys, breeders of the great Nisaean horses, who united under a judge-king, helped bring down Assyria, and whose priestly tribe, the Magi, gave their name to magic.
source: Herodotus, Histories book 1; Assyrian annals; the Babylonian Chronicle of the fall of Nineveh (612 BCE)

belligerent: shot three arrows from the saddle at full gallop and hit with all three
devout: kept the sacred fire alight through a whole winter of storms
cautious: settled a feud between two villages that had lasted three generations

inventions.name: Nisaean Horses
inventions.source: Herodotus and later writers praised the great horses of the Nisaean plain in Media, fed on 'Median grass' (alfalfa)
inventions.desc: Big, strong horses bred on alfalfa: everyone travels 8% faster and carries 1 more.

inventions.name: Mounted Archery
inventions.source: Cyaxares reorganised the Median army into spearmen, archers and cavalry (Herodotus 1.103)
inventions.desc: Archers who shoot from horseback and ride away: +2 attack.
inventions.hint: Needs Beast Domestication, and hunters led well.

inventions.name: The Seven Walls
inventions.source: Herodotus 1.98: Ecbatana had seven rings of walls, each painted a different colour, the innermost silver and gold
inventions.desc: Rings of walls rising up the hill, white, black, purple, blue, orange, silver and gold: +2 defence, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs Polished Stone Tools and the Tribe & Agrarian Era.

inventions.name: Fire Altar of the Magi
inventions.source: The Magi were a Median tribe of priests (Herodotus 1.101); fire altars appear at Median sites such as Nush-i Jan
inventions.desc: A fire that is never allowed to go out, tended by the priestly clan: rites bring 15% more devotion.

foods.name: Dried Curd Balls
foods.desc: Soured milk dried into hard balls that keep for a year on the march: food spoils 10% slower, hunger grows 5% slower.

foods.name: Saffron Broth
foods.desc: A golden broth coloured with crocus threads: +2 mood, the hurt heal 5% faster.

finds.name: Median Grass
finds.source: Alfalfa came to Greece from the Persian Wars, and the Greeks called it 'Median grass' (medike)
finds.desc: Deep-rooted purple-flowered fodder that makes horses grow big. Finding it brings domestication closer.

finds.name: Saffron Crocus
finds.desc: Autumn crocuses whose red threads colour food gold and ease pain.

people.name: Mitraka
people.desc: She can tell a foal's worth by the way it stands.
memory: raised a colt that grew taller than any horse in the valley

people.name: Varaza
people.desc: He sleeps with his bow strung and his horse saddled.
memory: drove off raiders from the hills with nothing but a bow and a fast horse

people.name: Mandane
people.desc: A Median princess whose father dreamed a vine grew from her and covered all Asia, and so married her to a quiet Persian. Her son was Cyrus.

people.name: Zarathustra
people.source: The Gathas of the Avesta; his date and homeland are still argued over
people.desc: The prophet who taught that the world is a struggle between truth and the lie, and that each person must choose good thoughts, good words and good deeds.

people.name: Madyes
people.source: Herodotus 1.103–106: the Scythians under Madyes ruled Asia for 28 years
people.text: a wild rider from the northern steppe, with a gold-covered quiver and a cup made from a skull.
memory: rode from the frozen north to the borders of Egypt
people.desc: A Scythian chief whose riders, Herodotus says, swept across the Near East.

people.name: Deioces
people.label: Deioces the Judge
people.desc: So fair a judge that the villages make him king. Lore 7.

people.name: Cyaxares
people.label: Cyaxares, who Took Nineveh
people.desc: He gives the Medes an army and brings down Assyria. Combat 8.

people.name: Harpagus
people.label: Harpagus the General
people.desc: A general who never forgets a wrong. Combat 6, Lore 4.

events.title: The Judge Who Would Be King
events.source: Herodotus 1.96–101: Deioces won fame as a fair judge, then refused to judge unless the Medes made him king
events.text: Quarrels between families are getting out of hand. The best judge among us says he will no longer settle them unless we give him a guard, a house on the hill, and the right to be seen only through messengers.

options.label: Make him king
options.result: A house rises on the hill, and the quarrels stop. Hardly anyone sees the judge any more.

options.label: Find another judge
options.result: The quarrels go on, but no one has to bow.

events.title: The Riders from the North
events.source: Herodotus 1.106: Cyaxares invited the Scythian chiefs to a feast, made them drunk and killed them
events.text: Riders from the steppe have come down on the valleys. They take a share of every harvest and ride off laughing.

options.label: Pay the tribute
options.result: The riders take their share and leave us in peace, for now.

options.label: Invite them to a feast

do.remember: poured the wine at the feast where the riders' chiefs fell

options.result: The wine flows, and the riders' chiefs never ride home. It is not a deed to be proud of.

options.label: Fight them in the open
options.result: The warriors ride out. The steppe riders are already circling.

events.title: The Great City Falls
events.source: In 612 BCE the Medes and Babylonians sacked Nineveh, the capital of Assyria
events.text: The great city of our old oppressors has fallen to our warriors and their allies. Its palaces burn; its carvings of kings lie smashed.

tales.name: The Dream of the Vine
tales.text: The old king dreamed that a vine grew from his daughter's womb and spread its leaves over all of Asia. The Magi told him: her son will rule in your place. So he married her far beneath her, and when the child was born he ordered it left on the mountain. But the herdsman's wife had just lost her own baby, and she kept the prince.

tales.name: Why the Fire Must Not Die
tales.source: Iranian fire worship, later Zoroastrian tradition
tales.text: Fire is the son of the Wise Lord, the brightest of all things, and the lie cannot bear its light. As long as one fire burns in the land, the darkness cannot win. So the Magi feed it day and night, and cover their mouths so that even their breath cannot defile it.

tales.name: Good Thoughts, Good Words, Good Deeds
tales.source: The Avestan creed humata, hukhta, hvarshta
tales.text: Two spirits were there from the beginning, twins: the better and the bad, in thought, in word, in deed. Between them the wise choose rightly, the foolish do not. Every person, every day, chooses which one to walk with.

tales.name: The City of Seven Colours
tales.text: On the hill of Ecbatana the walls rise one inside the other, each higher than the last: white, then black, then purple, blue and orange, and the two innermost covered in silver and in gold. From the plain, at sunset, the whole hill shines like a rainbow.
tales.moral: beauty is a kind of strength
